description: Look up the reservation; verify ID; authorize the card; assign a room; encode key cards
process_owner: Hotel General Managers (Resort Front Office Managers at the resorts)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 400 arrivals a day, mostly 15:00 to 22:00; a 4-hour outage in that window builds lobby queues of 40 or more parties at each resort; guests without rooms is the worst reputational outcome
manual_workaround: Printed arrivals and in-house lists (night audit plus every 4 hours at the resorts); paper registration cards; emergency pre-encoded key cards; P2PE devices in standalone mode at the resorts
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-09
dependent_third_parties: SYS-01 vendor; franchisor (SYS-02); payment gateways; SD-WAN provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Front desk agents; resort front offices; Hotels 3 to 6 front desks
quantified_operational_impact: About 167 resort arrivals and 236 select-service arrivals a day; manual check-in takes about 3 times longer
quantified_regulatory_impact: Guest register must still be kept for every arrival (Fla. Stat. 509.101(2)); back-enter within 24 hours

description: Encode key cards and mobile keys; cancel lost keys; issue master and emergency keys; keep lock audit trails
process_owner: Resort Chief Engineers; Hotel General Managers at Hotels 3 to 6
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Guest safety: new guests cannot get keys and lost keys cannot be cancelled; existing cards keep working offline; 2 hours is the longest the hotels can rely on escorted entry
manual_workaround: Emergency key cards held by the front office manager; staff escort with mechanical override keys; log every manual entry
dependent_systems: SYS-08; SYS-01 and SYS-02 interfaces; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: Door lock vendor (resort servers and the Hotels 3 to 6 cloud service)
quantified_operational_impact: 1,160 locks; about 400 new key sets a day; about 30 lost-key cancellations a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Lock audit trails are evidence in guest safety incidents
regulatory_driver: N72-R02 (15 U.S.C. 45(n) guest safety and security practices)

description: Deposits; authorizations; incidentals; check-out settlement; refunds; virtual card charges
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $214,000 of room revenue a day settles through the front desks; folios not settled at check-out are hard to collect; card compromise triggers acquirer and brand notice
manual_workaround: Resorts: P2PE devices in standalone mode and later folio posting; Hotels 3 to 6: brand gateway portal; never write card numbers on paper
dependent_people_or_facilities: Front desk agents; night auditors; Director of Finance
quantified_regulatory_impact: Card compromise duties under the merchant agreement and Visa rules (P08)

description: Booking engine, channel manager, online travel agency connections, and the brand central reservation system; rate and inventory updates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Lost or duplicate reservations cause overbooking because online travel agencies keep selling from stale inventory; about $214,000 a day of room revenue is booked through these channels
manual_workaround: Stop-sell on channels through vendor portals; take phone bookings on paper without card numbers and call back
dependent_third_parties: Booking engine vendor; channel manager vendor; franchisor; online travel agencies
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,050 reservations created or changed a day; about 30% of bookings missed in an 8-hour outage are not recovered
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; total price display rules still apply to manual quotes (16 CFR 464.2)

description: Phone bookings for the resorts, group pickup calls, and changes; card numbers keyed into SYS-01
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 900 calls and 210 bookings a day (about $33,000 of room revenue a day); callers book elsewhere when the line is down
manual_workaround: Route calls to resort front desks; take details without card numbers and call back
quantified_operational_impact: About 300 calls handled in 8 hours; about 40% of lost bookings are not recovered
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; call recording consent (Fla. Stat. 934.03) and card data in recordings (P10)

business_process: Resort food, beverage, spa, and retail service and payments
description: Order entry; kitchen tickets; outlet payments; spa bookings; room charges posted to folios
process_owner: Resort Directors of Food and Beverage
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $57,000 a day of outlet revenue across both resorts; room charges must reach folios before check-out
manual_workaround: Paper checks; Resort 1 P2PE devices in offline mode; Resort 2 imprint-free manual process: take cards only on standalone P2PE loaner devices, never on paper; post room charges later
dependent_third_parties: POS vendors; P2PE solution provider; processor
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,100 outlet transactions a day; 8 hours down is about one-third of a day's outlet business
quantified_regulatory_impact: Resort 2 outlets are in the cardholder data environment (not P2PE)

description: Group contracts; banquet event orders; deposits; group billing; master accounts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Events are booked weeks ahead; deposits can wait a few days; event-day changes need the banquet event orders
manual_workaround: Work from printed event orders; payment links for deposits; no card forms by email
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 events a week across both resorts
quantified_regulatory_impact: Card authorization forms in mailboxes are stored card data (Req 3.2, 3.3.1)

business_process: Night audit, accounting, and card settlement
description: Close the business day; settle card batches; post revenue; daily reports; guest register
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Card batches must settle within the acquirer's window to avoid higher fees; the day close drives reports and the guest register
manual_workaround: Run night audit late; settle batches from the gateway portals
dependent_third_parties: SYS-01 vendor; franchisor; payment gateways; acquirer
quantified_operational_impact: About $274,000 of daily revenue to post
quantified_regulatory_impact: Guest register kept in chronological order and available for inspection (Fla. Stat. 509.101(2))

description: Room status updates, housekeeping assignments on tablets, work orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rooms not marked clean cannot be assigned; late room readiness delays check-in
manual_workaround: Paper room boards; radio updates; printed assignment sheets
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,000 occupied rooms a day to clean and track

description: CCTV monitoring, emergency notification, in-house lists for evacuation, incident reports
process_owner: Director of Loss Prevention and Safety
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hotels must be able to account for guests during an evacuation or hurricane; CCTV gaps weaken incident response
manual_workaround: Printed in-house lists every 4 hours at the resorts and at night audit at Hotels 3 to 6; added security patrols
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,200 guests in house on an average night
quantified_regulatory_impact: Emergency evacuation duties; CCTV evidence requests

description: AI rate recommendations and automatic publishing (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rates can stay unchanged for a few days with limited revenue effect; switching AI-001 off is a safe response to a pricing problem (P10)
manual_workaround: Revenue managers set rates manually in the channel manager and brand system
quantified_operational_impact: Rates for 6 hotels and 365 future dates
quantified_regulatory_impact: During a declared state of emergency, prices are limited by Fla. Stat. 501.160

description: Resort websites, chatbot (AI-002), guest CRM, email campaigns, pre-arrival messages
process_owner: Vice President of Sales and Marketing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Guests must be reachable before arrival, especially for hurricane updates
manual_workaround: Website notice banner; phone tree from the in-house and arrivals lists; chatbot off with a phone number
dependent_third_parties: Chatbot vendor; web agency; email service vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 chatbot conversations and 40,000 emails a month
quantified_regulatory_impact: FTC Act Section 5 accuracy of statements; 16 CFR 464 total price in chatbot quotes

description: Time capture on 14 finger-scan clocks; biweekly payroll; onboarding; terminations; applicant screening
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; a missed payroll has legal and retention effects
manual_workaround: Paper time sheets; repeat prior payroll through the payroll vendor
dependent_third_parties: HR and payroll vendor; staffing companies
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment duties; background-check report disposal (16 CFR 682.3)

description: Vendor setup, invoices, payments, bank detail changes
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payments can wait several days; bank detail changes are a fraud target
manual_workaround: Manual payments for critical vendors with call-back verification

business_process: Financial reporting and owner and lender reporting
description: Month-end close, lender covenants, and (from 2027) REIT owner reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly cycle; lender and owner reports have contractual due dates
manual_workaround: Use prior-month reports and manual extracts
quantified_operational_impact: 6 hotels closed each month; 2 managed hotels from 2027
quantified_regulatory_impact: Management agreement reporting duties from 2027 (SOC 1 and SOC 2 commitments, P09)

description: Guest internet, meeting room internet, and TV
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Group contracts at the resorts promise meeting room internet; outages bring credits and reviews
manual_workaround: Cellular hot spots for meeting rooms; credits
dependent_systems: Guest Wi-Fi and TV networks (vendor-managed, outside the PMPS)
dependent_third_parties: Guest Wi-Fi and TV vendor; internet providers
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,200 guests and up to 1,000 meeting attendees a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Network separation from staff networks supports PCI scope
